headline: No live signal. Full 24-trade ledger still net -2.7 bps/trade (-64.4 total); last 10 bets +8.4 bps, mostly regime-lucky shorts.
regime_note: BTC has jumped to ~$78.8k, far above the $63-66k range that generated most of the ledger. The recent green run is a cluster of shorts fired into the Aug 21-23 pullback — regime-favorable timing, not evidence of durable edge.
assessment_md:
**Status: no trade signal right now, and the sample is still too thin to draw firm conclusions.**

**The full picture is unflattering.** Across all 24 resolved trades the strategy is net **-2.7 bps per trade (-64.4 bps total)** with just a **37.5% win rate**. That is consistent with the pre-live warning: gross edge is tiny (~4 bps) and realistic costs (~3 bps here) eat most or all of it. This is a marginal, likely-not-net-profitable signal.

**What changed vs last time:** little of substance. The rolling window (now 10 bets, +8.4 bps net, 90% win) still looks good, but it is the *same* cluster of shorts fired during the Aug 21-23 selloff — including two big winners (+48.7 and +16.2 bps). Strip out that regime-friendly pullback and the edge disappears. One trade (-60.9 bps on Jul 31) alone swamps many small wins.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us:** 24 trades is a handful, not a verdict. The recent green streak does *not* prove the edge is back — it proves shorts work when price falls. The negative full-ledger total does *not* prove the strategy is broken either; it's within noise for a 4-bps signal. Also notable: **zero survivors** in the independent edge search at 5 bps cost.

**Bottom line:** neither degrading enough to alert nor validated enough to trust. Treat as marginal-to-unprofitable, watch the full ledger, and don't be seduced by a short regime-driven hot streak.
